races.name: William Hill Epic Boost Fillies' Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Forest Berry
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's filly arrives on a 12-day turnaround with back-to-back wins, has a hood, and holds the solo front-running role here; her style-fit score reflects she is catalogued as prominent rather than a pure leader, but in this field she is the only one likely to clear to the front cleanly, making her the pivotal horse around which the entire race shape revolves.
runners_data.comment: Forest Berry arrives here in the form of her life, winning her last two starts, and with her trainer firing at 35% over the past fortnight, conditions look ideal; she has run over today's trip and going before, and carrying 137 lb from stall 8, she is the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Woodhay Wayfarer
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane partners this Tom Ward filly who landed a course-and-distance win on Good ground last time and has shown she can race up with the pace; 30 days between runs is not a concern for the trainer's record, and she should slot in just off Forest Berry to give herself the best chance if the race develops into a sprint finish.
runners_data.comment: Woodhay Wayfarer comes into this on the back of a win last time out and has experience over today's trip and going, but two fifth-place finishes before that win and a rating of 74 suggest she faces a stiff test against stronger rivals here.

runners_data.name: Greek Symphony
runners_data.note: Mason Paetel (3lb claimer) rides for Oliver Cole and this filly has been remarkably consistent, placing in four of five starts including a win over this trip at Standard going — her sim-going record of 1W1P in five matches the conditions perfectly and she looks tailor-made for a race run at a controlled pace where her finishing kick can be deployed off the leader's heels.
runners_data.comment: Greek Symphony shaped as a serious threat here, third last time out and a winner three starts back, returning on a quick 22-day turnaround with distance experience and a lively rating edge over her mark; the weight burden of 133 lb is the one factor to overcome.

runners_data.name: Pequenita
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding sends Oisin Murphy out on this filly whose natural front-running instinct will be constrained by the volume of prominent horses in the field — she has only three runs to her name and her best effort was a runner-up on this AW surface, so the question is whether Murphy can find a workable position if shut out of her preferred spot in the early stages.
runners_data.comment: Pequenita has shown consistent placing form, finishing second last time out and third two starts back, and has run over today's trip and going before; yet to score in her last three starts and a middle-of-the-road ranking here suggest she faces a stiff task at the weights with 131 lb to carry.

runners_data.name: Crazy Cubana
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's filly showed she could win (6f, Good) but her more recent efforts include a 17th and a 19th at Goodwood, suggesting top-of-the-ground conditions away from this surface may not suit; she is a front-runner by nature but is mapped back into midfield given the traffic, and on 37 days off she carries some unknowns about freshness.
runners_data.comment: Crazy Cubana brings solid recent form into this, her third placing two starts back a clear sign of ability, with a win four starts back underlining her class; the worry is that unplaced effort last time out leaves fitness on a retrieval mission after 37 days away.

runners_data.name: Magnesium
runners_data.note: Rossa Ryan takes the ride on John Butler's filly who holds a Standard-going win at 6f and is a genuine hold-up type stepping up in trip; 42 days off is worth noting, and she needs the pace to be genuinely testing to reel in those ahead of her — the controlled tempo Forest Berry is likely to set is not the scenario she requires.
runners_data.comment: Magnesium has going experience to call on and a win three starts back to advertise her claims, with our rating of 80 putting her among the principals. The risk is two unplaced efforts since that victory suggest she needs to rediscover that form.

runners_data.name: Attack Attack
runners_data.note: Liam Wright (3lb claimer) partners this George Scott filly who has headgear (blinkers) fitted and showed her best form with a fifth last time from her wide draw; a hold-up profile over a mile at Kempton on a steady pace is a difficult ask, and her form figures of 0035 suggest she is still finding her feet at this level.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked seventh of eight on our figures, Attack Attack faces a stiff task here; the 44-day absence is a concern, though a third two starts back offers a slender crumb of encouragement.

runners_data.name: Golden Oasis
runners_data.note: Rob Hornby rides for Robert Edwards (0/1 in 14 days) and this filly won over 7f on Good going but has a U in her recent form; like Pequenita and Crazy Cubana she prefers to be up with the pace, and having been running only 10 days ago she arrives fresh — the redistribution away from her favoured position is the key structural obstacle to her winning.
runners_data.comment: Golden Oasis unseated last time out and, ranked bottom of the field on our figures, is hard to fancy here despite a win two starts back and experience over today's trip and going.

races.paceDynamic: Forest Berry is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger likely to press her hard from the outset, she should be able to dictate at a controlled, sustainable gallop around Kempton's flat, right-handed polytrack mile. Greek Symphony, Woodhay Wayfarer and Pequenita are all prominent types who will want to race up with the pace, but the field contains more horses seeking that territory than the race shape can accommodate — Pequenita, Crazy Cubana and Golden Oasis are genuine up-with-the-pace runners who are all likely to find themselves shuffled wider or further back than their natural style demands. The result is that Forest Berry gets an uncontested lead at a Standard/Slow tempo, which on a flat Kempton AW mile typically produces a race where the front or prominent positions are protected and hold-up horses are asked to close on a wall of horses with a reserve of energy still intact. This shape strongly favours horses racing prominently or just off the lead — those who can track Forest Berry within a length or two and pounce in the straight — rather than genuine hold-up types who face traffic and a lack of strong pace to aim at.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Forest Berry Controls Unopposed
scenarios.trigger: If Forest Berry bowls along in front without serious pressure, setting a steady-to-moderate gallop that sees the field string out in file.
scenarios.body: Forest Berry takes the field along at a manageable tempo on the flat Kempton circuit, meaning her stamina reserves are barely tested and she remains full of running into the straight; horses prominent enough to track her — Greek Symphony and Woodhay Wayfarer — are ideally placed to mount the only credible challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Forest Berry sets only a crawl and one of the tracking prominent horses quickens past her in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A very slow early pace compresses the field and turns the race into a sprint from the home turn, suiting horses with a turn of foot who have sat just off the leader; Greek Symphony's consistent placed form and Woodhay Wayfarer's course-and-distance win both become relevant in this sharper-finish scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to string the field out and the front-runners tie each other up, allowing Magnesium or Attack Attack to close from the back.
scenarios.body: Magnesium has won over standard ground and Attack Attack showed improvement last time, and both sit at the tail of the field ready to benefit if the pace unexpectedly quickens and depletes those up front; however this scenario relies on a tempo that the lone front-runner is unlikely to set uncontested, making it the least structurally favoured shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Among Prominent Movers
scenarios.trigger: If crowding and jostling for position among the redistributed prominent types causes interference or checks early, scrambling the race shape entirely.
scenarios.body: Pequenita, Crazy Cubana and Golden Oasis all want to race up with the pace but cannot all do so cleanly, and any scrimmaging could unbalance some runners and create openings for those who settle quietly; this is a low-probability scenario but one where Oisin Murphy's experience on Pequenita could prove decisive if she threads through late.

watchPoints.text: Forest Berry's early manoeuvre is critical — if she breaks cleanly and clears the field within the first furlong, she controls the race; watch whether any of the three redistributed prominent types (Pequenita, Crazy Cubana, Golden Oasis) attempt to follow her and create an unexpected duel that collapses the dominant scenario.

Crazy Cubana and Golden Oasis both carry style-fit discounts and are likely to find themselves in an awkward middle ground — if either rider forces the issue for position in the first two furlongs, there is a risk of interference among the prominent group that disrupts Greek Symphony or Woodhay Wayfarer.

Magnesium and Attack Attack both need a truly run race to close from the rear; if Forest Berry controls the tempo at a steady Standard/Slow clip, watch whether either jockey attempts an early move rather than waiting for a late run that may never materialise.

The Standard/Slow going report is consistent across all distances today at Kempton AW, suggesting a slightly deadening surface that may favour horses who save energy in the early stages — worth noting for Forest Berry's sectionals in the final furlong if she has been pressed harder than anticipated.

Mason Paetel takes a 3lb claim on Greek Symphony — if the pace is moderate and the race turns into a two-furlong dash, his ability to time the challenge precisely from a tracking position will be under scrutiny, but the filly's consistent placed form suggests she is forgiving enough to compensate.

races.name: William Hill London Mile Series Final Handicap Stakes (Series Final - Qualified Horses Only)

runners_data.name: Two Tempting
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in a 14-runner field; Jonathan Portman stable in fair form at 1/21 over 14 days, has placed twice at Standard Kempton over the mile and simply needs to take advantage of its uncontested lead — though its role as pace-setter rather than finisher tempers expectations if the field closes late.
runners_data.comment: Two Tempting arrives in fine fettle just 14 days since his last start, has experience of today's trip and conditions, and our rating just edges him to the head of this field — the risk is that he remains winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Popmaster
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old prominent type who has placed at 9 of 15 visits to Standard going, but recent form reads 270446 and the absence of a win on this surface in recent starts raises questions about whether this handicap mark still represents a live opportunity for Ed Walker's charge.
runners_data.comment: Popmaster has shown consistent ability in recent starts, finishing fourth twice and fourth again three runs back, and his experience over today's trip and going counts in his favour; drawn 13 and carrying 136 lb, he has the profile to outrun his official mark of 96, though he remains yet to score in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Supido
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse tackling Standard Kempton for one of few times in his profile (just 3 visits in similar going), headgear flag noted; Ian Williams runner whose best form (1/8f/GOO) came on a contrasting surface, so the going is the principal query here.
runners_data.comment: Supido arrives here on a sound fitness pitch after 27 days off, has run over today's trip and going before, and a rating of 98 gives him a realistic shot from stall 10 off 134 lb; the main concern is that he has been unplaced on his latest start.

runners_data.name: Nikovo
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy picks up the ride on this consistent 7-year-old who has placed at 5 of 9 comparable-going starts and won on Standard ground recently; hold-up style suits a race where the pace is likely to be even rather than truly strong, and the booking of Murphy is noteworthy.
runners_data.comment: Nikovo won last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, so there are clear positives, though he carries 132 lb and his rating of 95 ranks him fifth of fourteen, suggesting he faces a stiff enough task against the principals.

runners_data.name: Cavolo Nero
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's 4-year-old has won twice on Standard going and twice on Soft at the mile trip, making this going profile a genuine strength; prominent style puts Kaiya Fraser in an ideal tracking position behind Two Tempting, and the OR of 92 with recent form of -23411 shows upward momentum.
runners_data.comment: Cavolo Nero arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and has experience of both today's trip and going, making him a compelling threat here; the danger is that 132 lb is a stiff burden to carry.

runners_data.name: The Liffey
runners_data.note: Hayley Burton's 5-year-old carries the best recent winning record in the race (four wins in last eight Standard outings) and is proven over the mile at this type of going; Rossa Ryan takes the ride on a horse fitted with tongue-tie and bit, and the 38-day gap since last run is the only query.
runners_data.comment: A winner four times in his last six starts with a runner-up effort last time out, The Liffey arrives here 38 days fresh and has experience of today's trip and going; however, his speed rating of 78 and ranking of seventh in a 14-runner field suggest he faces a stiff ask at the weights with 131 lb to carry.

runners_data.name: Percy's Lad
runners_data.note: Prominent-style 8-year-old wearing a hood, with a win on Standard ground at 7f and a placed effort at 8f on a similar surface in recent history; Ebrahim Nader's booking and the stable's 0/5 in the 14-day window suggests limited market confidence, though the OR of 89 is workable.
runners_data.comment: Percy's Lad won two starts back but was fifth last time out, and while he has run over today's trip and going before, a mark of 89 and 129 lb from stall 2 make life no easier for a gelding whose recent form has been inconsistent.

runners_data.name: Dingle
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's 8-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse that the pace map has shifted to midfield — the field simply has too many runners who want to be out the back; a 72-day absence is significant, and the recent form of 173000 shows form has tailed off sharply since spring.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 12 of 14 on our figures, Dingle has been unplaced in his last three starts and a winner six starts back, with 72 days off the track adding to the concerns; experience over today's trip and going is at least something to cling to.

runners_data.name: I'm Workin On It
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's 4-year-old holds the most compelling similar-going record in the race (4 wins, 7 places from 13 runs on Standard going) and a 68-day absence may have freshened him; prominent style suits the expected race shape, and the 126lb weight is manageable at OR 86.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 11 of 14 on our figures and fourth last time out after 68 days off, I'm Workin On It is hard to fancy at the weights off 126 lb; his one win in recent starts came four starts back, with only a second three starts back to add since.

runners_data.name: Exposure
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden's 4-year-old is a natural prominent type that the map has pushed to midfield due to congestion at the front — with just 1 run in comparable going from 7 attempts, the going profile is also a concern; discount slightly given the likely positional compromise.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Exposure does at least bring distance experience and a lively fitness edge at 17 days since his latest run, where he finished third two starts back; a rating of 90 gives him fair claims, though consistency remains the concern.

runners_data.name: Warrior Mode
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's 4-year-old has won twice on Standard/All-Weather going and placed three more times from only 5 similar-ground starts — a strong profile; prominent style is likely to secure a position just behind Two Tempting, and the recent 1 from 2 strikes makes this a live contender.
runners_data.comment: Warrior Mode won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, with a trainer firing at 35% in the last fortnight; however, he has been unplaced in one of his last five starts and his speed rating of 77 gives pause for thought.

runners_data.name: Blue Prince
runners_data.note: David Evans' 5-year-old is a natural prominent horse but the map has him displaced to midfield given the crowded front-running space — that positional squeeze is a real risk; unremarkable on Standard going with 0 wins from 7 similar-ground starts, despite a bold overall record.
runners_data.comment: Blue Prince won two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, but that seventh last time out is a concern, and he carries 124 lb from stall 14 with our rating suggesting he holds a slight edge over his official mark.

runners_data.name: Victory Ace
runners_data.note: John Butler's 3-year-old arrives on a four-timer, all on Standard surfaces and three at the mile trip — the form reads 265111 and the confidence is obvious; hold-up style means Finley Marsh will need a genuine gallop to launch, but the recent evidence suggests raw ability to overcome a positional disadvantage.
runners_data.comment: Victory Ace ranks last on our figures and his speed rating leaves him with plenty to find against these rivals, making him hard to fancy on ratings alone; that said, he has winning form in his last three starts and has experience of today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Vincent Rocks
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's 4-year-old is a true hold-up horse that the field size has forced into a midfield position on the pace map — 1 win from 8 similar-going runs and a visor in the headgear suggests a horse that needs things to fall right; 42-day absence and Warren Fentiman's claim are interesting if overlooked.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 13 of 14 on our figures, Vincent Rocks faces a stiff task, and a trainer striking at just 4% in the past fortnight does little to encourage; experience over today's trip and going, plus a second two starts back, offer slim comfort.

races.paceDynamic: Two Tempting is the one confirmed front-runner here and, critically, is uncontested — with no genuine rival likely to press from the outside, this 7-year-old should be allowed to establish a clean, controlled lead through the first half of Kempton's round mile before turning into the straight. The field does contain more prominent-leaning horses than the pace map can accommodate at the front — Exposure, Blue Prince, and to a lesser extent Warrior Mode are all natural prominent types who will be competing for a small number of positions in the first five, meaning at least one or two will find themselves racing in an unfamiliar midfield berth, compromising their chance. With Two Tempting setting a measured, sustainable tempo on Standard/Slow ground, the race is likely to develop into a steadily-run affair with a strong final-furlong kick rather than a stamina test — this shape disproportionately favours horses who travel smoothly in midfield or just off the pace and can sustain a run from the two-pole, giving an edge to prominent-to-midfield types with finishing speed over true front-runners or deep hold-up horses who need a strong pace to reel in.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Kick Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Two Tempting dictates uncontested from the front and the pace is just honest enough to string the field out without inviting a late mass surge.
scenarios.body: Two Tempting sets a comfortable tempo, hits the straight with daylight, and proves hard to reel in on Standard/Slow ground; horses just off the pace who travel into contention smoothly are the main danger as they can exploit any slow-down without needing a strong gallop.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Pace, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the early tempo is just brisk enough to set up a final-furlong finish for horses held up or tracking in third to fifth.
scenarios.body: The Liffey and Nikovo, both proven on this type of surface and coming from off the pace, are ideally placed to exploit a finish that rewards those who have conserved energy through the race; Victory Ace's recent winning streak on Standard surfaces makes it a live threat switching from the back.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Runner Holds
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is deliberately slow and the field dawdles into a sprint finish where position at the top of the straight becomes decisive.
scenarios.body: Two Tempting's uncontested lead becomes even more valuable in a sprint scenario, and Cavolo Nero — a two-time winner on Standard ground at this distance — has the tactical speed to be close enough to dominate.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage, Hold-Up Lands
scenarios.trigger: If the cluster of natural prominent types create early interference or jostle for position, stringing the race out and benefiting the deepest held-up runners.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape given that Exposure, Blue Prince, and Dingle are all racing at least partially out of their natural position and cannot be relied upon to create the strong pace needed to set up a deep hold-up winner; Victory Ace is the one hold-up type with the form to capitalise if the scenario does materialise.

watchPoints.text: Two Tempting's uncontested lead is the pivotal factor — watch the first two furlongs to see whether any of the nominal midfield starters (Warrior Mode, Cavolo Nero) push forward to press, which would transform the race shape entirely.

Victory Ace's rapid four-race winning run on Standard going is the most potent form line in the race — if Finley Marsh can slot in midfield with cover and the pace is honest, this 3-year-old has the raw ability to upend the field regardless of scenario.

I'm Workin On It holds the strongest comparable-going record statistically (13 runs, 4 wins, 7 places on Standard) and returns after 68 days — watch market moves in the morning; a significant drift would suggest the layoff is a genuine concern, a firm move the opposite.

Nikovo with Oisin Murphy is a combination that merits attention — Murphy rarely takes non-competitive rides in handicaps of this nature, and the horse's recent form (854331) shows a horse returning to form sharply over the right trip.

The cluster of Exposure, Blue Prince, and Warrior Mode all wanting to race prominently in the same ground could create a flashpoint early in the straight bend — any crowding or checking from that group may benefit horses like The Liffey or Cavolo Nero who settle quickly behind the early pace.

races.name: William Hill September Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Dubai Future
runners_data.note: Veteran ten-year-old hold-up performer trained by Saeed bin Suroor who recorded a recent course win over 16f; suited by a truly-run race and needs cover to deliver his finish, making him vulnerable if this stays tactical.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, and a winner three starts back, Dubai Future arrives here with mixed recent form but experience over today's trip and going working in his favour; the burden of 136 lb is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Almeric
runners_data.note: Progressive Andrew Balding four-year-old stepping up from 10f who has been consistently placed at Goodwood; prominent style maps well to this race shape and Rob Hornby's tactical ride could prove decisive tracking Gethin.

runners_data.name: Constitution Hill
runners_data.note: Nicky Henderson's nine-year-old has won twice on this course at shorter but has had a 164-day absence; a natural front-runner by inclination who cannot secure that position in this field and will need to adapt — the layoff adds further uncertainty to a role he will be asked to fill from further back than ideal.
runners_data.comment: A lengthy absence of 164 days is the obvious concern, and ranked last of six on our figures he faces a stiff task, though back-to-back wins in his last two starts and experience over today's trip and going offer some crumbs of comfort.

runners_data.name: Gethin
runners_data.note: The one confirmed pace-setter in this field; Owen Burrows has placed him well recently with a Sandown win on Standard ground, and from a prominent stall Callum Rodriguez can dictate terms without being pushed — his primary concern is whether his stamina holds over 1m4f having run most of his career at 10f.
runners_data.comment: Gethin shaped with plenty of credit when runner-up two starts back and was a winner three starts back, so the ability is not in question; he acts on today's going, but that 63-day absence is the one factor to weigh against him.

runners_data.name: Pride Of Arras
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's hold-up specialist found 12f at Goodwood this summer beyond him on his penultimate run but won over that trip on Good ground at Goodwood earlier; 42 days since last run and a return to similar conditions makes him interesting, though he needs a truly-run race to produce his best late effort.
runners_data.comment: Pride Of Arras shaped well last time, finishing second, and returns here 42 days on having run over today's trip before; carrying 133 lb is a stern ask, but his overall profile makes him our preferred pick in this six-runner contest.

runners_data.name: Tornado Alert
runners_data.note: Dual-purpose Suroor runner with wins at 8f and 10f who has shown ability to travel prominently; good Polytrack record with a Standard-ground win banked, and Oisin Murphy's booking lifts the profile — well-positioned to press Gethin and capitalise if the leader fades.
runners_data.comment: Tornado Alert won two starts back and was runner-up three starts back, showing consistent front-rank form at this level, and he has experience over today's trip carrying 133 lb; the concern is whether his fourth last time out represents a return to top form.

runners_data.name: Warrant Holder
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden's four-year-old has won on Tapeta and Standard surfaces and carries a good track record at 12f; a genuine prominent racer by nature who is pushed into a midfield mapping in this field because of the cluster of pace horses, so his chance is dependent on whether he can recover a more forward berth than the race shape strictly allows.
runners_data.comment: Warrant Holder has been out of the frame in his most recent start and, ranked fifth of six on our figures, is hard to fancy here, though he does bring distance and going experience to the table and showed a winner's instinct two and three starts back.

races.paceDynamic: Gethin is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only one genuine pace-setter in a seven-runner field, he shapes to dictate a controlled, pressure-free tempo from the front over Kempton's flat Polytrack mile-and-a-half. Callum Rodriguez can nurse him into a comfortable rhythm around the sweeping bends, meaning the pace is likely to be honest but not scorching, favouring a horse that travels well behind him rather than one that needs a truly searching gallop to produce a sustained finish. Tornado Alert and Almeric are the logical on-the-pace pursuers who will track Gethin, giving the mid-division types Dubai Future and Pride Of Arras a clearly defined target to chase. This race shape heavily favours prominent racers or those who travel close enough to the pace to pounce in the straight, rather than those required to produce a late burst from rear — the field holds more prominent-profile horses than the race can accommodate at the front, and Gethin is most likely to secure the rail lead ahead of Tornado Alert and Almeric; Constitution Hill and Warrant Holder, both natural front-runners by history, are mapped to midfield and are unlikely to secure their preferred position, meaning their chances are materially discounted in a shape that will not be truly end-to-end.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Gethin Dictates, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Gethin leads uncontested at a controlled tempo and the race develops into a test of tactical speed in the straight.
scenarios.body: Gethin sets a comfortable pace through the first mile, allowing Tornado Alert and Almeric to travel sweetly just off his shoulder before the pressure builds inside the final two furlongs; this shape rewards horses racing prominently at a sustainable gallop who can quicken on the Kempton straight rather than grinders needing a brutal pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the front group burns up the pace in a tactical battle between Gethin and Tornado Alert, creating a truly-run race that opens the door for the hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Dubai Future and Pride Of Arras, racing in rear with cover, pick up the pieces if the pace genuinely quickens early enough to expose the front-runners; this scenario is possible but requires a pace dynamic that the presence of a lone front-runner makes unlikely.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Disrupted Pace, Closers Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If Gethin is crowded or loses his rhythm at the start, scrambling the anticipated race shape and producing a more end-to-end contest.
scenarios.body: A messy early pace would bring Dubai Future and Pride Of Arras into the reckoning late, as a faster-than-expected gallop stretches the prominent brigade; the redistribution of Warrant Holder and Constitution Hill into midfield means this scenario also flatters horses not in their natural position, reducing its reliability.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Dominant Front-Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so negligible that Gethin simply steals an unassailable lead and the field cannot claw him back.
scenarios.body: A truly dawdling gallop on Standard/Slow Polytrack could see Gethin coast clear and resist all challengers into the straight; this outcome depends on Callum Rodriguez judging the fractions perfectly and the closers leaving it too late, but with Tornado Alert pressing close it is the least likely scenario.

watchPoints.text: Gethin's stamina at 1m4f is unproven at this level — watch whether Callum Rodriguez is able to coast at a safe pace or is pressed into a faster early tempo that could see him empty late.

Constitution Hill's 164-day absence combined with racing out of his natural front-running role creates a compounding risk — monitor his pre-race appearance and early positioning to assess whether Nicky Henderson has him primed.

Warrant Holder will attempt to push forward despite being mapped to midfield — if Benoit de la Sayette forces him up alongside Gethin it could turn the race into a tactical speed test that blows the field apart.

Saeed bin Suroor runs two in this race (Dubai Future and Tornado Alert) — watch for any stable-hand signals at the start that might indicate which is the preferred runner, as the trainer's 1/4 14-day record suggests targeted placement.

The going is Standard/Slow throughout the card — horses with proven Standard Polytrack form (Gethin 1W, Warrant Holder 2W, Tornado Alert 1W) carry a meaningful surface edge over those whose best form is on turf good ground.

races.name: William Hill Sirenia Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Adaay of Scarlett
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner at OR 106 under Rossa Ryan for Hugo Palmer; consistent front-runner with five consecutive placed efforts at 6f, though all on Good or Soft and this Standard/Slow AW surface is a going question mark — hood worn.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent and classy, Adaay of Scarlett has finished second on four occasions in recent starts and a winner six starts back, returning here fit on a 15-day turnaround having run over today's trip; the main risk is that fifth last time out suggests he may just find one too good again.

runners_data.name: Agamemnon
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes has strong recent form (T14: 4/28) and Finley Marsh takes over; recorded his sole win on Standard (AW) at 6f and placed again at that trip on Soft, giving genuine similar-going credentials that make this surface credible.|
runners_data.comment: Placed second two starts back and third three starts back, Agamemnon arrives on a sharp 15-day turnaround in solid recent trim, and has run over today's trip before; the fourth last time out is the one form line that gives slight pause.

runners_data.name: Moonrise
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy is a significant booking for Andrew Balding's unexposed two-year-old, who is unbeaten in three starts including a win on Standard AW — the strongest similar-going profile in the field; the 42-day break is the only flag.|
runners_data.comment: Moonrise arrives on the back of a win last time out, with another victory three starts back and experience over today's trip and going — a compelling profile. The main risk is the 42-day absence at 129 lb from stall nine.

runners_data.name: Social Symbol
runners_data.note: Crisford yard is quiet (T14: 1/23) and Social Symbol's recent form shows a drift from an opening win to back-to-back fourths; wants to be prominent but will face fierce early competition for the lead in this deeply contested pace scenario.|
runners_data.comment: Third last time out and a winner four starts back, Social Symbol arrives here in good heart after 28 days off, has run over today's trip, and his 102 rating makes him an appealing pick to go one better from stall 7 carrying 129 lb.

runners_data.name: Tawakal
runners_data.note: Second Crisford runner, lightly raced after just two starts with a win and a runner-up — both on Good ground at 6f; prominent style should see it involved, and the unexposed profile could mask more ability than the OR of 93 suggests.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of nine on our figures, Tawakal faces a stiff ask under 129 lb from stall 1, though he has run over today's trip and arrives on the back of a win and a runner-up finish in his last two starts.

runners_data.name: Bated Benevolence
runners_data.note: Marco Botti team in form (T14: 4/14) and owns similar-going experience at 6f on Standard AW; however a disastrous 16th in the Brocklesby on Good flags inconsistency, and the front-running style means it will be caught up in early pace traffic.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked eighth of nine on our figures, Bated Benevolence faces a stiff ask, though she arrives on a sound note — a runner-up last time out and a winner two starts back — and has run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Efsixteen
runners_data.note: Lightly raced (just two runs), with the sole win over 5f on Good — both a trip extension and a surface shift to AW required here; tongue-tie worn and front-running style puts it in the firing line of a chaotic early pace battle, creating significant risk.|
runners_data.comment: Winner two starts back but only fourth on her most recent outing, Efsixteen returns after 22 days and has run over today's trip before; the 126 lb burden and a ranking of sixth of nine in our ratings are the checks on her claims.

runners_data.name: Evenfall
runners_data.note: George Boughey's two-from-two juvenile is a genuinely quick horse whose wins at 5f and 6f on Good show smart early form; naturally prominent in style but placed to the rear of this mapping through field redistribution — if forced to race at the back, this is not its optimal scenario.|

runners_data.name: Nicely
runners_data.note: Won two of four including back-to-back wins at 6f on both Soft and Good, suggesting versatility; Kevin Philippart De Foy sends this out 14 days after its last run, and as a confirmed lead-seeker it will compete hard for supremacy but OR 89 makes it vulnerable if pace proves costly.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked well down the field on our figures despite an official mark of 89, Nicely has won twice in her last four starts and returns on a quick turnaround from stall two, with experience over today's trip adding mild encouragement, but the speed rating of 79 leaves her hard to fancy at this level.

runners_data.name: Shimmering Sun
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace has no runners in the 14-day window (T14: 0/14) and Shimmering Sun's last three runs have been below par — a 14th, a 7th, and a 2nd, though the sole win came at 5f on Good; the prominent style suits if pace collapses but current form is uninspiring.|
runners_data.comment: Shimmering Sun returns after 16 days carrying 126 lb from stall 6, and has run over today's trip before. A winner four starts back, she was second two starts back, but has disappointed on her most recent outing, leaving her profile a touch mixed.

races.paceDynamic: Five horses with genuine front-running habits — Adaay of Scarlett, Social Symbol, Nicely, Bated Benevolence, and Efsixteen — will all want to lead from the gates on this flat Kempton AW 6f, guaranteeing a strong, contested gallop from the outset on Standard/Slow going that will stretch stamina reserves. The early battle for supremacy between these five will create a pressured, honest fractions race where the front rank is unlikely to coast, and by the time the field turns into the straight, leaders will have burned significant fuel. This race shape strongly favours prominent-to-midfield horses with a proven cruising speed over 6f who can sit just off the frenzied pace and pounce in the final furlong — Moonrise, Agamemnon, and Shimmering Sun fit that profile best. The field holds more front-running types than can genuinely all get their position; of the five leaders, Adaay of Scarlett (highest OR, proven pace) and Nicely (recent winning form) are best placed to actually secure a front berth, with Social Symbol, Bated Benevolence, and Efsixteen all likely to be shuffled back or forced to race wider under pressure.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Stalkers Win
scenarios.trigger: If the five-way pace battle burns out the leaders, allowing the prominent stalkers to stride through late.
scenarios.body: The intense early duel between Adaay of Scarlett, Nicely, and Social Symbol sets suicidal fractions that unravel in the final furlong, leaving the race to those who tracked just behind with energy intact. Horses that can settle in the slipstream and quicken once the pace dissolves are perfectly suited to this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Setter Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If one front-runner — most likely Adaay of Scarlett — clears the pace traffic early and dictates a controlled but fast enough tempo that tests the field.
scenarios.body: With a high OR of 106 and proven 6f front-running ability, Adaay of Scarlett is best equipped to take advantage if rivals baulk or miss the break, setting a rhythm that proves just hard enough to repel closers on the AW surface.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Race, Class Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is surprisingly moderate and the race becomes a test of class and finishing speed in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A slower tempo would compress the field and turn the race into a sprint from two out, favouring the highest-rated horses who can produce a sharp turn of foot regardless of position; Moonrise's unbeaten record and Agamemnon's course-form at this exact trip make them standouts.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly brutal and every prominent runner fades, theoretically leaving a late closer to swoop from the rear.
scenarios.body: This shape is heavily discounted because Evenfall — the horse nominally mapped to a hold-up role — is a natural prominent racer redistributed rearward purely by field composition, meaning it is unlikely to produce a genuine late run from off the pace; no true hold-up specialist exists in this field to capitalise.

watchPoints.text: Moonrise, Agamemnon, and Tawakal are all tracking the same ground 2-3 furlongs out as multiple prominent horses contest the same racing room — traffic risk is acute and could cost any of them a clear run at the vital moment.

Adaay of Scarlett must win the early battle with Nicely, Social Symbol, Bated Benevolence, and Efsixteen for a front berth — if forced wide or checked at the break, its high OR advantage is significantly undermined.

Evenfall is genuinely unbeaten and fast but is mapped to race out of its natural prominent role; if Billy Loughnane takes it back under instruction to exploit the pace, watch whether it is happy settling — a change of running style cold could flatter to deceive.

Efsixteen steps up in trip to 6f for the first time on an AW surface it has never encountered — both variables arriving simultaneously in a race this competitive make it a horse to monitor rather than rely upon.

The Standard/Slow going (confirmed across all races on the card) will add a stamina premium to this 6f and may expose any runner without proven form at this trip on this surface — Moonrise's AW win at 6f is a notable differentiator.

races.name: William Hill Price Boosts Every Day Fillies' Handicap Stakes (London Sprint Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Zighy
runners_data.note: Prominent racer in fine nick (form 323 in last three, winner LR at Standard going), Billy Loughnane a strong booking and George Boughey's yard running at 1/23 in 14 days — course-going sim record of 2W3P underlines the suitability of this surface and trip, headgear worn (p).
runners_data.comment: Zighy arrives in sound nick after a third last time out, and a winner five starts back, with experience over today's trip in her favour; 135 lb and a trainer firing at just 4% in the past fortnight are the checks against her here.

runners_data.name: Lady Roxby
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who has been well beaten on softer ground recently (three 7ths on good) but posted a pleasing third at Standard Kempton last time; 43 days off the track is a mild concern, and Jack Mitchell will need significant pace collapse ahead to deliver her challenge from the back.
runners_data.comment: Rated marginally top of these on our figures, Lady Roxby has run over today's trip and going before and draws stall two carrying 135 lb; the concern is a string of sevenths and a ninth in her last four starts leaves her yet to win in recent outings.

runners_data.name: Powdering
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type dropping back after a 14th of 14 on soft, but recorded a course win at 6f on good ground and returned a third here recently; Seamus Cronin takes off 5lb which is significant, though Michael Herrington's yard is 3/15 in 14 days and she needs things to fall right from the rear.
runners_data.comment: Third two starts back and a winner three starts ago, Powdering arrives in decent recent form, though she was well beaten last time out; she has run over today's trip and going, carries 135 lb from stall one, and her rating of 83 offers mild encouragement.

runners_data.name: Tarot
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner, won over 6f at Standard Kempton on last visit but has since finished sixth twice; headgear (h) suggests keenness is managed, and Roger Varian's 4/19 stable form is solid — the concern is that Veil Of Clouds will not give this lead away cheaply and a prolonged battle could undermine both.
runners_data.comment: Tarot won four starts back and her rating of 87 marks her out as a strong player in this field, with experience over today's trip and going adding to her claims from draw 11; the worry is that she has finished sixth, sixth and seventh in her last three starts.

runners_data.name: Eskimo Pie
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly whose sole win came over 6f on good ground and whose AW form shows a placed effort at 7f Standard; Daniel Muscutt is a quality booking, trainer Jane Chapple-Hyam 0/12 in 14 days is a gentle flag, but she is a clean hold-up profile who could benefit from genuine pace.
runners_data.comment: Eskimo Pie catches the eye on the back of a win last time out, and at 24 days between runs she arrives fresh and ready to go. She has experience of today's distance and going, and 134 lb from stall 10 looks workable for a filly this in-form.

runners_data.name: Shallow
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up operator pushed into a midfield map slot because there are more true hold-up horses than positions — her natural racing style is further back than shown here, and the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) reflects that she is unlikely to get her preferred position; recorded three runner-up finishes on good at 6f suggesting she has the ability if everything clicks.
runners_data.comment: Shallow has finished second three times in her last six starts and returns in good order just 15 days after her latest runner-up effort, carrying 134 lb from stall 8 with experience of today's trip and conditions; the main risk is that she remains winless in recent starts and will need to finally convert.

runners_data.name: Paradise Walk
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with two wins at 5-6f on good and a placed effort at Standard AW; Rossa Ryan is a strong booking for Ralph Beckett whose yard is running at a dominant 8/42 over 14 days — she carries the headgear flag (b) and shapes as a natural second-rank mover who can quicken.
runners_data.comment: Two consecutive wins three and four starts back give Paradise Walk some credibility, but she has been unplaced on her latest outing and, ranked ninth of eleven on our figures, the weight of evidence makes her hard to fancy at the weights.

runners_data.name: Veil Of Clouds
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with excellent AW course profile (1W3P from four Standard starts) and Oisin Murphy taking the ride, which is the most significant jockey upgrade in the race; headgear (t) worn, 19 days between runs is fresh enough, and the Simon & Ed Crisford yard ticking over at 1/23.
runners_data.comment: Veil Of Clouds won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, but she carries 131 lb from stall four and her trainer has struck at just five per cent in the past fortnight, which tempers enthusiasm despite that recent victory.

runners_data.name: Calling A Star
runners_data.note: Prominent type who has won twice at 6f (including on Standard AW) and hit the frame on this surface before; Finley Marsh rides, Richard Hughes sending her from 38 days off — the 4/28 trainer strike rate in 14 days is modest but the horse's own AW record (1W2P from three) makes her very relevant here.
runners_data.comment: Calling A Star won three starts back but has since been out of the money, including an unplaced effort last time; she has run over today's trip and going, carries 131 lb from stall seven, and returns after 38 days off.

runners_data.name: Lope El Fuego
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who won over 6f on good ground on debut and has not reproduced that since (9th, 9th, 10th in subsequent runs); longest absence in the field at 58 days and Warren Greatrex's 4/13 14-day figure is reasonable, but the string of double-digit finishes makes this one to treat with caution until proven on AW.
runners_data.comment: Consecutive ninth-place finishes in her last two starts make Lope El Fuego difficult to fancy, ranked tenth of eleven on our figures, and 58 days off the track adds further uncertainty; she has run over today's trip and that third a few starts back hints at residual ability.

runners_data.name: Rumble Ruby
runners_data.note: Natural prominent runner with three wins and multiple places at 5-6f on good and Standard going — however, with so many forward-going horses in this field, securing a front-rank berth will be harder than usual, and Warren Fentiman (3lb claimer) rides for a yard at 1/7 in 14 days; its best chance depends on the pace thinning out ahead.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and carrying 129 lb, Rumble Ruby faces a stiff ask, though she does arrive third last time out, has run over today's trip, and her two wins in recent starts show she knows how to find the line.

races.paceDynamic: Tarot and Veil Of Clouds are confirmed front-runners who will contest the early lead from the off, creating a genuinely contested gallop across the Standard/Slow Kempton AW surface over six furlongs. With both horses drawn and motivated to stride forward, the pace figures to be honest rather than suicidal, but competitive enough to stretch the field and test those who cannot travel in behind. Zighy, Paradise Walk, Calling A Star, and Lope El Fuego will push forward for prominent positions, meaning this field carries more pace pressure than the map neatly accommodates — Rumble Ruby and Shallow are natural prominent and hold-up types respectively who are unlikely to secure their preferred position in this traffic. That early battle between Tarot and Veil Of Clouds combined with a congested chasing pack sets this race up as a test of tactical positioning and stamina through the final two furlongs, favouring horses who can travel just off the pace and quicken once gaps emerge — the prominent-to-midfield closers are structurally best placed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested lead, closers pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Tarot and Veil Of Clouds push each other along at an honest clip and the race opens up for those racing prominently to midfield in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Veil Of Clouds and Tarot fight for control but the sustained gallop drains both, leaving the door open for horses travelling smoothly in second rank; Zighy, Paradise Walk, and Calling A Star are ideally positioned to pick off a tiring leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Veil Of Clouds dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Veil Of Clouds (four wins and places on this exact surface) controls the tempo without excessive pressure and dictates to the line.
scenarios.body: Veil Of Clouds' strong course form (1W3P from four AW starts) makes her the most likely solo front-runner if Tarot is slow away or unable to match early strides; in a controlled scenario she proves very hard to peg back at this trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace collapse, hold-up horse strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the early battle burns out the leaders spectacularly and a genuine closer arrives late with a sustained run.
scenarios.body: Eskimo Pie or Lady Roxby, racing back in the field away from the scrimmage, would be the natural beneficiaries of a strong pace collapse; this scenario is moderately discounted because Shallow — a natural hold-up horse — is bumped forward in the map and unlikely to fill its ideal position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield grind, prominent wins
scenarios.trigger: If the going plays notably slower than Standard and the race becomes a stamina grind rather than a tactical sprint.
scenarios.body: Horses carrying less weight and racing prominently without overexerting early will grind past laboured leaders on the premises; this is the least likely shape given the pace dynamic but Rumble Ruby's natural energy, though mapped out of role, could still see it feature if the race steadies.

watchPoints.text: Veil Of Clouds and Tarot will clash for the lead from stall to the first furlong — watch whether Tarot is able to match Oisin Murphy-ridden Veil Of Clouds early, as any sustained battle between them directly increases the chances of the prominent-to-midfield horses (Zighy, Paradise Walk, Calling A Star) swooping late.

Rumble Ruby is a natural prominent racer that the map has redistributed to midfield due to field congestion — if Warren Fentiman elects to push forward regardless, watch for interference or crowding in the first two furlongs with multiple horses seeking the same early positions.

Paradise Walk carries the blinkers flag and has a powerful stable booking in Rossa Ryan for a Ralph Beckett yard in excellent recent form (8/42 in 14 days) — any market drift before the off from this runner deserves attention given the booking quality.

The going is listed as Standard but every race on the card is running Standard/Slow, suggesting the surface is playing slightly slower than the headline figure — horses who have proven stamina reserves at 6f AW (Veil Of Clouds, Calling A Star) may hold an edge over those at the top of their trip.

Eskimo Pie and Lady Roxby are the purest late-closers in the field and their finishing positions will be a direct barometer of how hard the pace was — if both close strongly, the front-runners were flattered by the shape; if neither makes ground, the pace was more controlled than expected.

races.name: William Hill Best Odds Guaranteed Handicap Stakes (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Haku
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up specialist in form (won 12f/STA last time, 7 days ago), Mark Loughnane yard in decent touch; excels on similar going but will need gaps to open in the straight from his rearward berth, and 1m4f is towards the outer edge of his best trip.
runners_data.comment: Third two starts back and a winner five starts back, Haku has solid recent form to build on, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; at 135 lb, the weight is the one factor to overcome.

runners_data.name: Astro King
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old with a headgear flag (p) and a deeply uninspiring AW record of zero wins from 15 similar-going starts; ridden by Ebrahim Nader and drops slightly in grade, but his recent form figures of 0/0054 suggest he is struggling to compete at this level.
runners_data.comment: Astro King heads this 11-runner field on ratings and shaped with fair merit when fourth last time out, though he remains winless in recent starts; back within a workable 16 days and carrying 135 lb over a trip he has tackled before, he is the one to beat.

runners_data.name: King's Code
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for David Evans, fitted with visor; won at 10f on Good and has shown enough over 12f to be credible at this trip; Alexandra McDonnell claims 7lbs, which matters, and his 9/15 hit-rate on similar going is solid — well placed to track Topteam throughout.
runners_data.comment: King's Code won three starts back and returns on a handy 23-day turnaround with experience of today's trip and conditions and a rating of 97 putting him firmly among the dangers; the worry is two consecutive eighths since that victory.

runners_data.name: Whitcombe Rockstar
runners_data.note: Genuine prominent type who won his last two starts (12f/STA and 11f/STA) and is clearly at home on this surface; 72 days off is a mild query but trainer Keiran Burke saddled a winner in the last 14 days, and from a prominent pitch he looks ideally placed to challenge late.
runners_data.comment: Whitcombe Rockstar won back-to-back races earlier in this sequence and ran a solid second three starts back, giving him a strong recent profile, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; the concern is 72 days off the track without a run since.

runners_data.name: Topteam
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner; Oisin Murphy partnership is a significant upgrade and Andrew Balding sends him out freshened after 98 days — his Kempton AW win (1/12f/STA) confirms the course/surface suits, and an uncontested lead on Standard/Slow ground is a potent combination.
runners_data.comment: Topteam was second two starts back and got off the mark four starts back, so the ability is there, but he comes into this unplaced last time and a lengthy 98-day absence to overcome, making him a fascinating if uncertain each-way proposition at a hefty 131 lb.

runners_data.name: Incensed
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Amanda Perrett who has placed three times over 12f on similar going but is yet to win at 14f, and this extended trip may just stretch his finishing effort; Daniel Muscutt rides and he needs a searching pace to be seen at his best — unlikely to get that against Topteam.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Incensed does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and her rating of 96 suggests more ability than her official mark of 89 implies, but an unplaced effort last time and a fifth before that are a concern at 129 lb.

runners_data.name: Majestic
runners_data.note: A true hold-up specialist by nature, though mapped to midfield here because the field contains more rear-runners than the race shape can accommodate; Jack Channon has two wins from 18 in the last 14 days and the horse has been placed over this course configuration, but his 0W1P from 15 AW starts is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Majestic shaped with promise when third last time out and has experience over today's trip, but he has been winless in his last five starts and that unplaced effort two runs back tempers expectations somewhat at a mark of 88.

runners_data.name: Primo Lara
runners_data.note: In excellent recent form (two wins from last four), Billy Loughnane takes the ride for Jane Chapple-Hyam; by instinct a hold-up horse, though crowded to midfield in this mapping — his raw ability is hard to ignore and the 12f trip on AW has suited him before, but he will need things to fall right positionally.
runners_data.comment: Primo Lara won two of his last six starts, including back-to-back victories two and three runs back, but he was beaten into fourth last time out and his speed figure of 79 leaves him needing to find more against stronger company here.

runners_data.name: Tiernan
runners_data.note: Four-year-old who won at 11f/GOO and placed at 10f/GOO in recent starts; Rossa Ryan is a strong booking for Iain Jardine, who is 3/25 in the last 14 days; a natural hold-up racer shuffled into midfield by the race shape, and a genuinely slow pace is his enemy rather than his friend.
runners_data.comment: Ranked ninth of eleven on our figures, Tiernan is hard to recommend despite a win two starts back; he was fifth last time out and his speed rating lags his other marks, leaving him a difficult proposition even at a workable weight of 125 lb.

runners_data.name: Elsass
runners_data.note: Has won over 11f and placed over 12f, so the trip holds no fear; Rob Hornby rides for Charlie Johnston (3/37 last 14 days); an AW hold-up horse by trade, his most recent form figures of 7-7-3 on Soft/Good suggest he is finding his level, and he will need a stronger pace than Topteam is likely to set.
runners_data.comment: Seventh in each of his last two starts, Elsass faces a stiff task ranked tenth of eleven on our figures, though he has run over today's trip and going before and his two wins in recent starts show he retains ability when conditions click.

runners_data.name: Sudu
runners_data.note: Four-year-old prominent racer trained by Roger Varian, who is in good form (4/19 last 14 days); only 2/7 on similar going and a form figure of 6 last time suggests he is not at his peak, but the step back up to 12f from 8f last time is a positive — Rowan Scott will try to make use of an early prominent position.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Sudu has finished sixth and eighth in his last two starts, making him hard to fancy despite a win three starts back and experience over today's trip.

races.paceDynamic: Topteam is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with Oisin Murphy in the saddle, will stride to the front from the off and control proceedings at a measured, sustainable gallop on this Standard/Slow Kempton AW surface over 1m4f. With no credible pace rival to force the issue, Topteam is free to dictate every inch of the race, likely setting a tempo that suits those in behind but keeping enough in reserve to kick again turning for home. The early-to-mid sections will be unhurried, meaning the race will be run as a largely processional exercise until the straight, where premium finishing acceleration matters most. This shape heavily favours prominent racers who can track Topteam without expending energy and quicken in the straight — King's Code and Whitcombe Rockstar fit that bill — while genuine hold-up horses will struggle to generate the ground-cover needed off a slow pace; Majestic, Primo Lara, Tiernan, and Elsass are all true hold-up types but are mapped to midfield because there are simply too many hold-up horses to accommodate at the rear, and of the prominent horses, King's Code and Whitcombe Rockstar are most likely to actually secure position just off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Topteam controls, track prominent
scenarios.trigger: If Topteam sets a steady, unchallenged pace and the race is won by a horse tracking close throughout the straight.
scenarios.body: Topteam leads at a measured clip, allowing King's Code and Whitcombe Rockstar to travel in behind before unleashing their kick in the Kempton straight; Standard/Slow going limits the sustained finish of hold-up horses and rewards those who were always travelling on the heels of the leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-runner holds on
scenarios.trigger: If the slow, uncontested pace allows Topteam to convert its lead position into an outright win at the line.
scenarios.body: Murphy, aboard Topteam, dictates fractions so modest that the chasing pack is never asked a question until too late; at 1m4f on a flat AW circuit, a horse allowed to coast can conserve enough energy to repel challenges in the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late closers charge home
scenarios.trigger: If a false, dawdling pace compresses the field and triggers a sprint finish that allows the best-finishing hold-up horse to pounce.
scenarios.body: A very slow early pace can paradoxically create a bunched sprint finale where a horse with genuine late acceleration can thread through; however this scenario depends on redistributed hold-up types (Majestic, Primo Lara, Tiernan) finding clear daylight, which is uncertain given they are not in their natural rearward position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield grinders prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slow enough to produce a stamina test in the final two furlongs rather than a speed finish, favouring the most durable stayer.
scenarios.body: Incensed and Sudu, who both stay the trip reliably and grind rather than quicken, could benefit if the race turns into a war of attrition; this is the least likely shape given the flat Kempton circuit and Standard/Slow going that typically rewards acceleration over raw stamina.

watchPoints.text: Topteam and Oisin Murphy — if Murphy elects to bowl along from the front completely unchallenged through the first mile, the lack of any pace rival could allow him to dictate such slow fractions that he simply does not stop in the straight.

King's Code (visor, prominent) and Whitcombe Rockstar — both have the profile to track Topteam and quicken; watch whether Alexandra McDonnell or Josephine Gordon gets the better position tracking the leader, as only one can sit sweetly on Topteam's quarters.

Primo Lara and Tiernan — both true hold-up horses compressed into midfield; if Topteam slows the pace dramatically early, they may find themselves trapped in a convoy with nowhere to go, which would severely reduce their chance of winning even if their raw form merits respect.

Haku's jockey Jack Mitchell — Haku won seven days ago and returns quickly; watch whether Mitchell tries to take closer order than Haku's usual hold-up berth, which could indicate connections feel the horse is in exceptional form and want to exploit it before an imminent handicap rise.

Sudu for Roger Varian — a prominent racer returning from 29 days off, and Varian's stable is 4/19 in the last 14 days; if Sudu travels fluently in the early stages alongside King's Code and Whitcombe Rockstar, he could inject an unexpected dimension into the prominent battle and complicate King's Code's position.

races.name: William Hill Keep Your Raceday Positive Handicap Stakes (London Stayers' Series Qualifier) (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Naval Tribute
runners_data.note: Wears a visor and has won twice over this 2m trip including at Goodwood; the sole front-runner here and likely to dictate, though racing out of his fully natural prominent role and fresh off a 96-day break — fitness and concentration through the final quarter-mile are the key questions.|
runners_data.comment: Naval Tribute arrives on the back of three wins in his last six starts, including a victory last time out, and has experience of both today's trip and going — he's no stranger to these conditions. The main risk is a 96-day absence.

runners_data.name: Barenboim
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old veteran with a mixed record over 16f on Standard going (1 win, 3 places from 10 runs in similar conditions); holds up naturally and relies on a genuine test of stamina that a Naval Tribute-led crawl is unlikely to provide, making it hard to see how he gets competitive.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts yet a step back to third two runs ago showed residual ability, and Barenboim's experience over today's trip and going, combined with a rating of 85 that tops this six-runner field, makes him the one to side with.

runners_data.name: An Bradan Feasa
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes over in the saddle for Jack Jones, a notable booking; consistently placed over 16f at Goodwood (four seconds and a third in last five), travels close to the pace, and the steady gallop here should allow him to conserve energy for a sustained challenge from 2f out.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent and lively coming into this, An Bradan Feasa has been runner-up four times in his last five starts, with a win five starts back, and arrives on a sharp 22-day turnaround with distance and going experience in his favour. The main risk is whether he can finally convert his placed efforts into victory.

runners_data.name: Betelgeuse
runners_data.note: Recent winner at Yarmouth and placed twice over 16f; his natural style is a genuine hold-up close to the tail of the field, but with multiple closers in this small field he is mapped to midfield — the compressed race shape risks leaving him without the room or pace to land a telling blow.|
runners_data.comment: Betelgeuse has been winless in his last six starts, and ranked last on our figures he faces a stiff task here, though he returns on a sharp turnaround of 14 days, has run over today's trip, and those placings show he can knuckle down.

runners_data.name: Campeona
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's three-year-old has won three of her last five and her record over longer trips (1m7f, 2m) is excellent; despite a natural hold-up style, her class advantage and trainer's track record of peaking horses precisely make her the most dangerous of the hold-up contingent if the slow tempo can be navigated.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked fifth of six on our figures and carrying 126 lb, Campeona looks to have plenty to find on ratings despite a lively recent sequence that includes three wins in her last five starts; she has run over today's trip and going, and her trainer is striking at 35% in the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Flash Kozo
runners_data.note: Won over 14f on Standard going and has placed at that trip in similar conditions; in truth a hold-up horse by inclination, but with several closers in this field he is mapped to midfield — Kaiya Fraser's claiming allowance saves 7lbs but the race shape pointing to a slow-run tactical test does not favour his style.|
runners_data.comment: Flash Kozo arrives in fine nick — a winner two starts back and second last time out, he handles today's going and comes here fresh off an 18-day break carrying 124 lb, though his speed rating of 65 is the main risk against stronger rivals.

races.paceDynamic: Naval Tribute is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of six over this 2m trip on Kempton's AW surface, and with just one horse willing to lead, the pace is expected to be steady and uncontested — a controlled, single-file procession that sets up a test of stamina and tactical positioning rather than raw speed. An Bradan Feasa will likely push up to sit prominent in second or third, giving Naval Tribute a shadow but no serious pressure, meaning fractions will be slow early and the race will compress into a tactical sprint from the home straight. Campeona, Barenboim, Flash Kozo, and Betelgeuse all carry hold-up profiles, but Flash Kozo and Betelgeuse are redistributed into mapped midfield positions — in reality this field has more closers than the rear of the race can accommodate, meaning those two are unlikely to get far enough back to produce their best finishes. The dominant race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently or close to the pace and produce a sustained finish, rewarding An Bradan Feasa's proven front-running proximity and Campeona's relentless staying form over pure hold-up operators waiting on a pace that may never materialise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Proximity Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Naval Tribute dictates a measured gallop unchallenged and the race ignites only in the final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: Naval Tribute sets a comfortable tempo and An Bradan Feasa tracks closely, both conserving energy for a late duel that rewards horses already in contention turning in; hold-up types are left with too little ground to make up against a slow-then-fast pace pattern.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Campeona Stealthy Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow enough that Campeona, despite a hold-up role, can travel with enough cover to produce her trademark sustained finish.
scenarios.body: Sir Mark Prescott's three-year-old has winning form over 16-17f and has been placed or won in five of her last five; a slow early gallop shortens the race effectively and her superior class rating relative to OR may allow her to sweep through late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Chaos Erupts
scenarios.trigger: If Naval Tribute's visor fails to hold concentration and the front breaks down, leaving the field bunched and the race a sprint finish from 2f out.
scenarios.body: A messy, stop-start gallop benefits whoever can find a clear run soonest from the home turn; Barenboim's experience over 16f on this surface gives him a sliver of hope if he can find daylight from the rear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Grind Through
scenarios.trigger: If an uncharacteristically strong early tempo develops and the pace tests stamina, allowing genuine hold-up types to pick off tiring rivals late.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires Flash Kozo or Betelgeuse to find their natural position at the back of a genuinely run race, but both are redistributed out of their preferred roles and face a likely slow pace that negates their finishing kick; the shape is possible but structurally unlikely given the runner profiles.

watchPoints.text: Naval Tribute's visor is crucial — if he switches off or loses the lead approaching the home straight, the entire race map unravels and An Bradan Feasa may find himself exposed in front earlier than ideal.

Campeona is drawn to improve significantly on her OR=74 mark; Sir Mark Prescott's runners often arrive cherry-ripe after short breaks, and her three-year-old allowance combined with a sustained gallop could make her look well-handicapped late in the race.

An Bradan Feasa has four consecutive second-place finishes over 16f — if he travels smoothly again but cannot find a winning effort, Naval Tribute or Campeona may be the ones to beat him to the line rather than a hold-up horse.

Flash Kozo and Betelgeuse are both true hold-up horses compressed into midfield by the field composition — watch whether jockeys Fraser and Wright attempt to push back to their natural positions early, which could create traffic issues on the back straight in a six-runner race.
